headline: Parliament in uproar after MP Hannan Masud accuses PM of making ‘false’ claims
summary: The National Citizen Party MP sparked a heated debate during budget discussions, criticizing the Prime Minister's remarks on the opposition's position.
details: A heated debate broke out in parliament today as National Citizen Party (NCP) MP Abdul Hannan Masud accused the Prime Minister of making “false” claims while criticizing the opposition’s position on the proposed 2026-27 budget.
Hannan Masud stated that the Prime Minister's claims—specifically that the opposition is protesting because liquor or cigarette prices have increased—are disheartening and false.
The MP further criticized the government's handling of loan defaults and the takeover of Islami Bank, claiming that the Prime Minister's remarks encourage loan defaulters.

Masud also expressed concern over the use of 'language of appeasement' toward India, echoing the rhetoric of the previous fascist regime, and described border killings as murder and a threat to sovereignty.
The remarks sparked loud protests from ruling party MPs, with LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir demanding that the accusation of 'false statements' be expunged from the parliamentary record.
Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman suggested that debating truth and falsehood within the House could become embarrassing for everyone, while Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal intervened to maintain order.
The Deputy Speaker announced that the matter would be reviewed and a decision will be taken after due consideration.
caption:
“The honourable prime minister is not present today. But we are deeply disappointed when he makes false claims.”

A heated debate broke out in parliament today as National Citizen Party (NCP) MP Abdul Hannan Masud accused the Prime Minister of making “false” claims while criticizing the opposition’s position on the proposed 2026-27 budget.

Hannan Masud stated that the Prime Minister's claims—specifically that the opposition is protesting because liquor or cigarette prices have increased—are disheartening and false.

The MP further criticized the government's handling of loan defaults and the takeover of Islami Bank, claiming that the Prime Minister's remarks encourage loan defaulters.

Masud also expressed concern over the use of 'language of appeasement' toward India, echoing the rhetoric of the previous fascist regime, and described border killings as murder and a threat to sovereignty.

The remarks sparked loud protests from ruling party MPs, with LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir demanding that the accusation of 'false statements' be expunged from the parliamentary record.

Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman suggested that debating truth and falsehood within the House could become embarrassing for everyone, while Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal intervened to maintain order.

The Deputy Speaker announced that the matter would be reviewed and a decision will be taken after due consideration.

headline: Former chief justice Khairul Haque denied bail in July Uprising murder case
summary: The 81-year-old former chief justice remains in jail after a Dhaka court rejected his bail petition in a murder case linked to the July Uprising.
details: A Dhaka court has denied bail to former chief justice ABM Khairul Haque in a murder case connected to the July Uprising. Judge (In-Charge) Sadekin Habib Bappi of the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge’s Court-7 rejected the petition, ensuring he remains in custody.
